introduction_markdown:
**Time allowed: three hours.** This paper contains six questions arranged in three sections: Section A - Physical and General Chemistry (questions 1 and 2); Section B - Inorganic Chemistry (questions 3 and 4); Section C - Organic Chemistry (questions 5 and 6).

Answer ALL the SIX questions in this booklet. The mark allocation is indicated for each question. Each question carries 20 marks. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Calculators may be used.

**Useful data:** one atmosphere (1 atm) = 1 Pa = $1.01\times10^{5}$ N m$^{-2}$ (as printed); relative atomic masses (RAM): C = 12.0, S = 32.0, O = 16.0, H = 1.0; molar gas volume at stp = 22400 cm$^3$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Define

(i) a chemical bond.

(ii) State and explain the shapes of the following molecules: $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and $\mathrm{BCl_3}$. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Chemical bond.** A chemical bond is the strong electrostatic force of attraction that holds atoms (or ions) together in a compound. It results from the rearrangement of outer-shell electrons: they are transferred (ionic bond), shared between nuclei (covalent bond) or delocalised among positive ions (metallic bond).

**(ii) Shapes** (valence shell electron pair repulsion theory: the electron pairs around the central atom repel one another and arrange themselves as far apart as possible).

- $\mathrm{NH_3}$: nitrogen has 5 outer electrons, 3 of which form N-H bonds. There are **3 bond pairs and 1 lone pair**, i.e. 4 electron pairs, arranged tetrahedrally. Only the three bonded atoms are seen, so the shape is **trigonal pyramidal**. A lone pair repels more strongly than a bond pair (lone pair-bond pair repulsion is greater than bond pair-bond pair repulsion), so the H-N-H angle is reduced from $109.5^\circ$ to about $107^\circ$.
- $\mathrm{BCl_3}$: boron has 3 outer electrons, all used in the three B-Cl bonds. There are **3 bond pairs and no lone pair**. The three pairs are furthest apart in one plane, so the shape is **trigonal planar** with Cl-B-Cl angles of $120^\circ$ (boron is electron deficient, with only 6 electrons in its outer shell).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Sodium-23 decays through $\beta$-emission and has a half-life of 12 days.

(i) What is meant by half life?

(ii) Write a balanced nuclear equation for the $\beta$-emission of sodium-23.

(iii) Calculate the mass that remains when a 1.25 g sample of sodium undergoes decay for 60 days. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** The half-life is the time taken for the amount (number of nuclei, hence mass) of a radioactive isotope to fall to **half** of its initial value; equivalently, the time for the activity to halve.

**(ii)** In $\beta^-$ emission a neutron changes into a proton, so the atomic number rises by 1 and the mass number is unchanged:

$${}^{23}_{11}\mathrm{Na} \rightarrow {}^{23}_{12}\mathrm{Mg} + {}^{\ 0}_{-1}\mathrm{e}$$

Mass number: $23 = 23 + 0$. Charge (atomic number): $11 = 12 + (-1)$. Both are balanced. (An antineutrino is also emitted.)

**(iii)** Number of half-lives $n = \dfrac{60}{12} = 5$.

Mass remaining $= 1.25 \times \left(\dfrac12\right)^{5} = \dfrac{1.25}{32} = 0.0391\ \mathrm{g}$ (about $0.039\ \mathrm{g}$).

Check: $1.25 \rightarrow 0.625 \rightarrow 0.3125 \rightarrow 0.15625 \rightarrow 0.078125 \rightarrow 0.0390625\ \mathrm{g}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
In an experiment to determine the molar mass of a volatile liquid, 1.715 g of a liquid was vapourized at $40^\circ$C and 2 atm releasing 488 cm$^3$ of vapour.

(i) State the experimental method used in the determination of the molar mass of the liquid.

(ii) Calculate the molar mass of the liquid. ($R = 0.082\ \mathrm{atm\,dm^3\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$). *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** The **Victor Meyer method** (vapour density method): a weighed sample of the volatile liquid is vaporised in a heated tube; the vapour displaces an equal volume of air, which is collected and measured at known temperature and pressure. (A gas-syringe method, in which the vapour volume is read directly, is the same idea.)

**(ii)** Convert to consistent units: $V = 488\ \mathrm{cm^3} = 0.488\ \mathrm{dm^3}$, $T = 40 + 273 = 313\ \mathrm{K}$, $P = 2\ \mathrm{atm}$.

From $PV = nRT$:

$$n = \frac{PV}{RT} = \frac{2 \times 0.488}{0.082 \times 313} = 0.0380\ \mathrm{mol}$$

$$M = \frac{\text{mass}}{n} = \frac{1.715}{0.0380} = 45.1\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$$

The molar mass of the liquid is about $45\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Potassium chlorate (V), $\mathrm{KClO_3}$ decomposes in the presence of manganese (IV) oxide catalyst to release oxygen.

(i) Write out a balanced equation for the decomposition of the chlorate.

(ii) Calculate the volume of oxygen produced (measured at stp) for the decomposition of 0.73 g of $\mathrm{KClO_3}$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** $2\mathrm{KClO_3} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{KCl} + 3\mathrm{O_2}$ (heat, $\mathrm{MnO_2}$ catalyst). Check: K 2 = 2; Cl 2 = 2; O 6 = 6.

**(ii)** The paper's data list does not give K or Cl; the standard values K = 39.0 and Cl = 35.5 are used.

$M(\mathrm{KClO_3}) = 39.0 + 35.5 + 3(16.0) = 122.5\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$

$n(\mathrm{KClO_3}) = \dfrac{0.73}{122.5} = 5.96\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{mol}$

From the equation, 2 mol $\mathrm{KClO_3}$ give 3 mol $\mathrm{O_2}$, so $n(\mathrm{O_2}) = \dfrac32 \times 5.96\times10^{-3} = 8.94\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{mol}$.

$V(\mathrm{O_2}) = 8.94\times10^{-3} \times 22400 = 200\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ at stp.

questions.enonce_markdown:
An ideal mixture contains 0.85 moles of methanol and 0.42 moles of ethanol. If the vapour pressure of pure methanol and pure ethanol at $20^\circ$C are 98 mmHg and 43.6 mmHg respectively.

Calculate:

(i) The mole fraction of each component in the mixture.

(ii) The partial pressure of each component.

(iii) The total pressure of the mixture. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Total amount $= 0.85 + 0.42 = 1.27\ \mathrm{mol}$.

**(i)** $x_{\text{methanol}} = \dfrac{0.85}{1.27} = 0.669$ and $x_{\text{ethanol}} = \dfrac{0.42}{1.27} = 0.331$ (they add up to 1).

**(ii)** Raoult's law for an ideal mixture: $p_i = x_i\,p_i^{\circ}$.

$p_{\text{methanol}} = 0.669 \times 98 = 65.6\ \mathrm{mmHg}$

$p_{\text{ethanol}} = 0.331 \times 43.6 = 14.4\ \mathrm{mmHg}$

**(iii)** Dalton's law: $P_{\text{total}} = 65.6 + 14.4 = 80.0\ \mathrm{mmHg}$.
